Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has announced his departure from the club with an emotional farewell message, thanking the Premier League side for supporting his development since he joined its academy in 2020. The 16-year-old shared a farewell video on his Instagram account, #jjnr10, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, reflecting on his six-year spell at the club and the memories he would cherish. In the video, Gabriel described his arrival at Manchester United as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams and highlighted scoring at Old Trafford and winning the Jimmy Murphy Award among his memorable experiences. “Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams. Here I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award. “You gave me moments I will always treasure. To every coach and every member of staff, to my teammates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ,” he wrote. Sky Sports also reported on Tuesday, that Gabriel had announced his departure, adding that Real Madrid had reached an agreement with Manchester United earlier in November to sign the teenager. The Spanish club is reportedly planning to bring him in during the January transfer window. Sky Sports However, Gabriel did not mention Real Madrid or identify his next destination in his farewell message. According to The Guardian, in a report published on November 17, Gabriel had been absent from Manchester United since requesting the cancellation of his registration in September, shortly before turning 16 on October 6. The newspaper also reported that Manchester United had “initially hoped to persuade the teenager to remain at the club but appeared to be preparing to explore legal options against his next club over possible breaches of regulations.” Gabriel joined Manchester United in 2020 and became the youngest recipient of the club’s Jimmy Murphy Award, presented to its young player of the year. He also made an appearance for the senior side in a pre-season friendly against Atletico Madrid in August, although he did not feature in a competitive first-team match. His final appearance for the club’s youth side appeared to be the UEFA Youth League fixture against Sabah on September 10, in which he scored a hat-trick in a 5-0 victory, according to The Guardian.
